segments.t: The File Browser is a dockable sidebar that browses your KTPH000localKTPH001 filesystem next to the terminal. It is laid out like the terminal's remote files sidebar: a KTPH002Local FilesKTPH003 title bar with the actions, the current folder as clickable path segments, a filter, and a listing of one folder with KTPH004NameKTPH005, KTPH006SizeKTPH007 and KTPH008ModifiedKTPH009 columns, type-aware icons and a status footer. (For browsing a KTPH010remoteKTPH011 server over SFTP, use the KTPH012SFTP file managerKTPH013 instead.)
Toggle the panel from the menu bar:
KTPH000View → File Browser → Show on LeftKTPH001
KTPH000View → File Browser → Show on RightKTPH001

Selecting the item again, or the KTPH000✕KTPH001 button in the panel's title bar, hides the panel. A draggable divider resizes it (280–900 px, 380 px by default); the window keeps that width instead of squeezing the panel when the terminal needs room. The panel's KTPH002position, width, Show Hidden Files setting and last directory are remembered across restartsKTPH003.

The listing shows one folder at a time. KTPH001Double-clickKTPH002 a folder (or select it and press KTPH003KTPH000KTPH004) to change into it; the KTPH005..KTPH006 row at the top goes up to the parent folder. The title bar's buttons:
Return to a previously visited directory
Show the parent folder (may go above your home directory)
Reload the folder shown, keeping the selection
Create an item in the folder shown

Choose the sort key (Name, Size, Date modified) and direction (Ascending / Descending); a click on the KTPH000NameKTPH001, KTPH002SizeKTPH003 or KTPH004ModifiedKTPH005 column header does the same, and a second click reverses the direction. Hidden entries (names starting with a dot) always stay at the top, then folders before files

Below the title bar, the KTPH008pathKTPH009 shows the folder as segments, starting at KTPH000 inside your home directory or at the filesystem root outside it; click a segment to go to that folder. Click beside the segments, or press KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011+KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013 / KTPH014KTPH004KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH005KTPH017, to type a path instead: KTPH018KTPH006KTPH019 goes there, KTPH020KTPH007KTPH021 returns to the segments. A leading KTPH001 expands to your home directory; absolute paths outside home are allowed. The KTPH022filterKTPH023 field below it narrows the listing to entries whose name contains the typed text (case-insensitive).
Directories load in the background, so a large or network-mounted folder no longer freezes the window; a brief loading indicator appears while a directory is read.
Open a file, or change into a folder
Go up to the parent directory
Delete the selection (choose Trash or permanent)
Type a path to go to
Right-click an entry for the full menu:
KTPH000OpenKTPH001 — open the file with the operating system's default application, or change into the selected folder.
KTPH000Open in Snippet EditorKTPH001 — load a text file (up to 10 MB) into the KTPH002Snippet EditorKTPH003.
KTPH002RenameKTPH003 — rename inline; a name clash is resolved by appending KTPH000, KTPH001, …
KTPH000CopyKTPH001 / KTPH002CutKTPH003 / KTPH004PasteKTPH005 — move or copy within the browser.
KTPH000Copy PathKTPH001 — copy the item's absolute path to the clipboard.

KTPH000DeleteKTPH001 — a confirmation prompt offers KTPH002Move to TrashKTPH003 or KTPH004Delete PermanentlyKTPH005. Moving to the Trash is reversible; permanent deletion cannot be undone. On a system without a Trash, only permanent deletion is offered. The deletion runs in the background so a large folder does not freeze the window.
KTPH000New FolderKTPH001 / KTPH002New FileKTPH003 — create an item.
KTPH000Set owner / group / permissionsKTPH001 — change ownership and POSIX permissions (where the filesystem supports it).
KTPH003ArchiveKTPH004 — pack the selection into a KTPH000, KTPH001 or KTPH002 archive.
KTPH000DetailsKTPH001 — show type, size, path, modification time and permissions.

Each row shows a KTPH002type-aware iconKTPH003 (folder, code, image, archive, document or executable), with a badge for symbolic links, its size (KTPH000 for folders) and when it was last modified. A name too long for the column ends in KTPH001; point at it to see the whole name in a tooltip, or select the entry (with a click or the arrow keys) to see it right below the row. The footer reports how many folders and files the folder shown holds and how many entries are selected.

Drag files KTPH001outKTPH002 of the browser onto another application to copy them, and drag files KTPH003intoKTPH004 the browser to copy or move them into a folder. Dropping onto a folder row targets that folder; dropping elsewhere targets the folder shown. Name clashes are resolved with a KTPH000 suffix rather than overwriting.
